title: It looked alive… but heaven found nothing.
paragraphs: It looked alive… but heaven found nothing.

Because some of us have mastered the language of faith…
but lost the life of it.

We carry titles.
We wear “Christian.”
We know how to lift hands, quote verses, post devotionals.

In , the image captures a moment we often skip past too quickly—Jesus approaching a fig tree that looked full, promising, alive. But Mark 11:13 reveals the truth: “When He came to it, He found nothing but leaves.”

Not broken fruit.
Not immature fruit.

The tree wasn’t pretending to be dead.
It was advertising life.

Because empty people don’t deceive.
But “almost fruitful” people do.

You can look right…
sound right…
even feel right in moments…
and still be disconnected from the life of Christ.
Some scholars interpret this fig tree as a symbol of outward religion without inward transformation—Israel appearing devoted, yet lacking true righteousness. But don’t miss it…
This is not just about a nation.

Have you ever prayed publicly with passion…
but privately felt distant?

Have you ever posted something spiritual…
while hiding something sinful?

Have you ever delayed obedience…
but justified it with “I’m still growing”?
That quiet compromise no one sees…
That hidden pride that says, “At least I’m better than before…”
Jesus didn’t curse the tree because it struggled.
He confronted it because it misrepresented.
God is not impressed by what you display if it doesn’t reflect what you’ve become.
Because we live in a time where visibility is mistaken for spirituality.
But heaven doesn’t measure your platform.
Galatians 5:22 doesn’t say the fruit of the Spirit is influence, followers, or recognition. It says it is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance.
Fruit is not what you show people.
Fruit is what remains when nobody is watching.
If your private life contradicts your public faith, you don’t have a fruit problem…
Because Jesus said in John 15:5, “I am the vine, you are the branches… apart from Me you can do nothing.”
So if there is no fruit…
It’s not because you need to try harder.
It’s because somewhere, you stopped abiding.
This is where many miss it.
We think fruit comes from effort.
You don’t force a branch to produce fruit.
You keep it connected to the vine.
And yet we exhaust ourselves trying to look alive…
Some of us are more committed to maintaining an image than cultivating intimacy with Christ.
Jesus didn’t come just to expose barren trees.
The same Jesus who cursed the fig tree…
went to the cross for fruitless people like us.
Romans 5:8 says, “While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
Not when we finally produced fruit.

Sin is real.
Brokenness is real.
Our inability to produce true righteousness on our own is real.

Jesus lived the life we couldn’t live.
Died the death we deserved.
And rose again so we could be made new—not just improved.
You are not called to fake fruit.
You are called to bear fruit.
And that only happens when your life is rooted in Christ.
If Jesus walked up to your life today…

Not tomorrow.
Not when you feel ready.

Confess what you’ve been hiding.
Surrender what you’ve been delaying.
Lay down the version of you that looks alive but isn’t.
And receive the grace that actually transforms.
If you feel that tug in your spirit—that’s not guilt trying to crush you.
That’s God calling you back to life.
Not hype. Just truth that feeds the soul.
We’re going deeper into what kills fruit silently.
